overall: Atlanta is in an active warming trend at 13:00 ET, with the running max at 82.4°F and still climbing at +1.7°F/hr — well below what GFS and ECMWF projected but with 2-3 hours of prime heating time remaining. The high dewpoint of 68.0°F indicates significant atmospheric moisture, which tends to moderate afternoon peak temperatures even under strong insolation. Morning warming was sluggish (75.2°F held through 9am), but the pace has been steady at roughly +1.8°F/hr since then.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is unusually wide: GFS at 92.0°F appears aggressive given the moisture load, NBM at 83.4°F looks too conservative given the current velocity still firmly positive at 1pm, and ECMWF at 87.6°F sits in the middle as the most plausible anchor. The Tier 2 ensemble signal (even model: 90-91°F) points toward the upper range, but the Tier 4 odd model signal (89-90°F, Avoid) tempers confidence in that zone.
max_temp_prediction: With 82.4°F already locked in at 13:00 and +1.7°F/hr velocity, simple extrapolation over a 2-hour remaining heating window suggests roughly 85-87°F before the rate tapers — consistent with ECMWF's 87.6°F guidance. The high dewpoint argues against the GFS 92°F ceiling, while the Tier 2 ensemble signal at 90-91°F provides some upside risk. Best estimate is approximately 87.5°F, with moderate confidence; key uncertainty is whether afternoon cloud cover or boundary-layer moisture caps the ascent below ECMWF or allows a push toward 89°F.
